title: Cash Handling & Daily Reconciliation
summary: Safely handle register cash, reconcile each drawer against Shopify POS, document variances, secure funds, and follow approved deposit procedures.
sections: Core cash policy

All cash transactions must be recorded through Shopify POS. Every register is reconciled daily; shortages and overages are documented immediately. Only authorized personnel may access the safe or prepare deposits.
Daily reconciliation

Count each register separately, leave a $500 BEGINNING BANK, compare Shopify POS EXPECTED to physical cash, use REMOVE CASH and CLOSE SESSION, print the receipt, wrap it with the cash, and secure it in the safe.
Variance & deposits

Recount and notify the Branch Manager immediately when a drawer does not balance. Deposits are generally prepared Fridays unless directed otherwise; bank runs go directly to the bank and require a validated receipt.

title: Delivery Procedure
summary: Standard delivery-driver workflow from clock-in through route completion, with safe driving, accurate delivery, customer service, material care, incident response, and return-to-branch requirements.
sections: Phase 1 — Start of day
Clock in, carry your driver license and company phone, review the delivery schedule and special notes, and ask questions before leaving when anything is unclear.
Phase 2 — Route packet

Meet with the Branch Manager and/or Warehouse Manager. Receive delivery invoices, route order, customer notes/call-ahead instructions, and confirm stop count, special handling, time-sensitive deliveries, and required equipment.
Phase 3 — Vehicle inspection
Complete the Box Truck Pre-Trip Inspection Checklist before operating any company vehicle.
Phase 4 — Load verification

Before moving the truck, verify material matches the manifest, counts are correct, customer orders are separated, fragile material is protected, doors/windows are padded, no material is loose, the lift gate is clear when applicable, and initial the manifest.
Phase 5 — Departure
Confirm sufficient fuel, review GPS, mount the phone, notify the manager, confirm the first stop, lock truck doors, adjust mirrors, and fasten the seat belt.
Phase 6 — On the road

Obey traffic laws, NEVER use handheld phones, wear seat belts AT ALL TIMES, drive defensively, maintain following distance, avoid aggressive driving, and observe roadway height/weight restrictions. Give customers about 30 minutes notice, or more if requested. Follow EasyRoutes, avoid unnecessary mileage and idle time, take the safest route, and take the 30-minute meal break. Extended delays require notification to the Branch Manager/Warehouse Manager and the customer or branch.
Phase 7 — At the delivery

Park safely, use hazards if needed, verify the address, review the delivery, unload safely, obtain a customer signature with NO EXCEPTIONS, photograph the delivery with NO EXCEPTIONS, and return the paperwork. Represent Bargain Moulding professionally: greet customers, be courteous, NEVER argue, NEVER discuss pricing, NEVER promise credits, and direct concerns to the branch.
Material handling

Carefully unload. NEVER drag doors/material across the floor or ground, NEVER throw material to a customer, do not carry more than you can safely handle, and stabilize the remaining load after each stop.
Damage, refusals & returns

If damage is discovered: stop unloading, photograph it, notify the Warehouse Manager and Branch Manager, document it on delivery paperwork, receive customer acknowledgement, then proceed with remaining material. If a customer refuses delivery, call the Branch Manager immediately, DO NOT leave material, wait for instructions, and retain the paperwork. Returned material stays on the manifest, remains secured, is inspected on return, and may return to racks if no visible damage exists.
Accidents & incidents
ANY ACCIDENT REQUIRES IMMEDIATE BRANCH NOTIFICATION. Secure the scene, call emergency services if needed, notify the manager, take photographs, complete an Incident Report, and DO NOT admit fault.
Phase 8 — Return to branch

Fuel the truck for the next day if required, unload returns, organize paperwork, discuss customer issues with the Branch Manager, report damaged material, clean the cab, remove trash, lock the truck, complete the post-route inspection, and clock out.
Code of conduct

Every driver represents Bargain Moulding from the time the truck leaves the yard until it returns. Operate safely, communicate professionally, protect company assets, and treat every customer with courtesy and respect. Delivery quality includes both accuracy and the customer experience.

title: Customer Returns, Store Credits & Refund Authorization
summary: Handle customer return requests with a solution-first approach while protecting sellable inventory and following approval requirements.
sections: Our approach to returns

The goal is not to shut down a customer request. Listen to the customer, inspect the material, and work toward an appropriate resolution while protecting Bargain Moulding inventory. When appropriate, the preferred order of resolution is MATERIAL EXCHANGE → STORE CREDIT → REFUND. Employees should not lead with harsh statements such as “NO RETURNS” or “ALL SALES ARE FINAL.”
Never promise before inspection

Never promise an exchange, store credit, or refund before the required physical inspection and approval. A good customer-facing explanation is: “We’re happy to take a look at the material and see what options are available. We need to inspect it first, and then we can determine the best way to help.”
Responsibilities

Sales Associates receive the request, verify the customer and original order/invoice information, explain the process positively, and coordinate inspection. The Warehouse Manager physically reviews returned merchandise and determines whether it is suitable for resale. The Branch Manager resolves disputes and exceptions and handles situations requiring management approval.
Physical inspection

Every return must be physically reviewed by the Warehouse Manager before the final resolution is determined. Verify SKU/product, quantity, overall condition, packaging when applicable, cuts or modifications, paint or stain, installation/use, water or handling damage, and whether the product can reasonably return to inventory as Grade A/resalable material. No separate inspection form is required.
Generally non-returnable material

Material generally cannot be accepted when it is damaged, altered or modified, installed, painted or stained, cut, used, customer-damaged, special order, custom-made, non-stock, clearance/closeout/final sale, or otherwise unable to be resold as Grade A inventory. Do not argue with the customer; explain the issue professionally and involve management when needed.
Special-order and production doors

Production door orders require a signed Door Production Authorization Form before manufacturing. Because these doors are manufactured specifically for the customer, they are normally non-returnable and non-refundable. Retain the signed authorization with the customer order and escalate exceptional circumstances to management.
Resolution 1 — Material exchange

After inspection and approval, first consider a material exchange when suitable replacement material can solve the customer’s issue. This is especially useful when the customer needs a different product, size, profile, or other replacement material.
Resolution 2 — Store credit

If an exchange is not appropriate, offer store credit when reasonable. Locate the customer profile in Shopify, verify customer information, enter the approved credit amount, confirm the credit appears correctly, and explain the available balance to the customer.
Resolution 3 — Refund

An approved return may be refunded to the original payment method when appropriate. Verify the original payment method, process the refund through Shopify, and document the reason and required approval. Company-caused issues such as incorrect material supplied or delivered, company-caused damage, or significant fulfillment errors should receive particular consideration toward making the customer whole.
Restocking fees

Approved returns may be subject to a restocking fee of up to 10% of the purchase price based on the condition, quantity, and nature of the returned merchandise. Employees must not invent or automatically apply a fee. Follow management direction when a restocking fee may be appropriate and explain it professionally.
Company errors and exceptions

Examples requiring additional consideration include the wrong item sold, wrong item delivered, company-caused damage, manufacturer defect, significant order-fulfillment error, or another management-approved circumstance. Focus on making the situation right rather than winning an argument over policy. Unusual exceptions and resolutions must be documented.
Restocking approved material

Inspect approved material again before returning it to inventory. Return it to the correct inventory location using proper inventory procedures. Isolate damaged or questionable material and complete an inventory adjustment when required. Only material appropriate for inventory should return to sellable stock.
Documentation

Maintain the customer invoice/order, photos when needed, manager approval when required, Shopify credit/refund documentation, inventory adjustments when required, and documentation supporting unusual exceptions. A separate return inspection sheet is not required.
Customer service standard

Remain professional. NEVER argue with the customer. NEVER promise an outcome before inspection. NEVER use the return policy simply to shut down the conversation. Listen, explain the inspection process, and work through the approved resolution options. The objective is to protect company inventory while making a reasonable effort to take care of the customer.

title: Damaged Material & Claims
summary: Identify, photograph, isolate, report, and properly resolve damaged material while preserving inventory accuracy and claim evidence.
sections: Core workflow
Identify → Photograph → Isolate → Report → Determine Disposition → Correct Inventory if Authorized.
Non-negotiable standards

Never conceal damage. Do not return damaged material to sellable inventory without approval. Do not discard material connected to an open vendor or freight claim without authorization. Employees may not independently promise customers refunds, replacements, discounts, or store credit.
Assess facts
Identify SKU, product, quantity, and related order number. Describe observable damage. When the cause cannot reasonably be established, document facts rather than assigning blame.
Photographs

Photograph the overall product, close-up damage, SKU/label, shipment and shipping label when applicable. For freight damage, photograph before breaking down the load when practical and safe. No separate damage inspection form is required.
HOLD – DAMAGED MATERIAL

Each location will maintain a designated physical area for damaged material that is waiting for management review or final disposition. This area will be identified as HOLD – DAMAGED MATERIAL. When practical, employees should move damaged material to this area so it is physically separated from normal sellable inventory. Material in this area is NOT AVAILABLE FOR SALE unless a manager later approves it for return to sellable inventory. When practical, identify the material with useful information such as SKU, quantity, related order number, date, and reason it is being held.
Vendor / PO damage

Do not receive a damaged shipment as though everything arrived correctly. Photograph and isolate affected material, identify SKU and quantity, retain relevant packaging when practical, notify the Director of Procurement, provide PO/supporting information, and follow Procurement direction for QOBLEX receiving.
Claims documentation

Procurement may manage vendor and freight claims using photographs, email, PO information, packing slips, Bills of Lading, vendor communication, claim references, credits, replacement information, and other records appropriate to the situation. No separate claims form is required. Keep claim material available until Procurement authorizes disposition.
Transfer damage

Photograph and document affected material, notify the originating Warehouse Manager and Inventory Manager, and follow the Inventory Transfer procedure. Do not automatically assign blame or simply absorb the loss.
Warehouse-caused damage

Accidental damage must be reported immediately. Damage identified → photographed → isolated → reported → disposition determined → inventory corrected if authorized. Accidents can happen; knowingly concealing or failing to report known damage is a separate compliance issue.
Order picking

Do not knowingly provide damaged material to a customer just to complete an order. Separate it, check for replacement inventory, notify the Warehouse Manager, document it, and move damaged material to HOLD.
Delivery damage

Stop handling affected material, photograph it, notify the branch, make no unauthorized customer promise, document the issue on existing delivery paperwork, and follow branch instructions and the Delivery Procedure SOP.
Customer-reported damage

Gather customer/order/product details, description of damage, photos when available, pickup/delivery status, and discovery timing. Do not immediately assume company or customer responsibility. Management reviews the facts and follows the Returns SOP when customer resolution is needed.
Final disposition

Possible outcomes include return to vendor, vendor credit, replacement, freight claim, approved return to sellable inventory, discount/as-is sale, company use, disposal, or customer resolution. Warehouse employees and Sales Associates do not independently determine final disposition unless authorized.
Inventory adjustments
Physical damage does NOT automatically authorize an inventory adjustment. Adjust only after disposition is determined and authorization exists. Follow Inventory Adjustments & IAL.
Escalation

Immediately escalate significant losses, repeated vendor/carrier damage, customer property damage, vehicle accidents, employee injury, disputed responsibility, suspected intentional damage, large inventory discrepancies, and safety hazards.

title: Customer Backorder Management & Resolution
summary: Document every customer backorder, communicate proactively, investigate availability, reserve material when it arrives, prioritize fulfillment, and keep the obligation open until the customer is fulfilled.
sections: Backorder mantra

A backorder represents an existing obligation to a customer — not a new order waiting to be scheduled. RESERVE IT. COMMUNICATE IT. DELIVER IT. CLOSE IT. Material received does not mean the backorder is resolved; customer fulfilled means the backorder is resolved.
Document every backorder

ALL backorders must be documented. Identify the customer/order, exact SKU and quantity owed, shortage, employee responsible for communication, electronic record, follow-up, and final resolution. The company computer system is the official record; the physical invoice in the Open Backorder Folder is the backup record.
Identify, verify, and notify

The Warehouse Manager verifies SKU, ordered quantity, physical quantity, normal storage and staged material before declaring a shortage. For deliveries, document SKU, description, quantity ordered, quantity delivered and quantity backordered on Driver/Route Paperwork and the Office Copy. Notify the Delivery Driver and Branch Manager before departure whenever possible.
Customer contact before delivery

The Branch Manager or designated employee makes every reasonable effort to contact the customer before an incomplete delivery arrives. Explain what is unavailable, quantity backordered, what will still arrive, that availability is being investigated, and that outstanding material from a company-created delivery backorder will be delivered FREE OF CHARGE once available.
Incomplete delivery and communication

Available material should generally continue on the scheduled route while unavailable material is managed as a backorder. Acknowledge the inconvenience, take ownership, explain what happens next, avoid speculation and unsupported promises, and never blame employees, departments, branches, vendors, manufacturers, or drivers to the customer.
Investigate and update

The Branch Manager coordinates with the Inventory Manager to investigate current inventory, other locations, transfers, incoming POs and known inbound inventory. The Director of Procurement may investigate vendors/manufacturers when needed. Never promise an arrival date without reliable support; communicate an ETA as an estimate unless confirmed. Keep the customer reasonably updated.
Review open backorders

Branch and Warehouse Managers use the computer system as the primary source. Daily review covers new backorders, expected material, immediate follow-ups, urgent project needs and orders ready for fulfillment. Weekly review covers aging orders, missing ETAs/follow-ups, newly available inventory, escalation and customer dissatisfaction.
When material becomes available

Backordered material becomes committed customer inventory and an immediate fulfillment priority. Verify SKU/quantity/customer, separate it immediately, label and stage it, notify the Branch Manager and update the electronic record. Do not return it to unrestricted stock or sell it to another customer before the existing obligation is addressed.
Fulfill with priority

Existing backorders take precedence over normal delivery scheduling. Delivery backorders go on the next practical route, are identified as BACKORDER FULFILLMENT, and receive no additional delivery fee. Pickup backorders are reserved, staged, labeled and the customer is contacted immediately.
Close only after fulfillment

Close a backorder only after the customer receives all outstanding material or another documented management/customer resolution is completed. A PO, transfer, ETA, material arrival, staging, customer contact, or scheduled delivery does NOT close it. Mark CLOSED / FULFILLED in the system, record resolution/date, then remove and retain the physical paperwork according to company procedure.

quiz.question: When is a customer backorder actually resolved?
answers: When the customer receives the outstanding material or another approved documented resolution is completed
When a purchase order is created
When the material arrives at the warehouse

quiz.question: What is the official tracking record for all customer backorders?

answers: Immediately reserve, label and stage it for the customer owed the material
Sell it to the next customer who asks

quiz.question: What should a customer be charged for delivery of material owed from a company-created delivery backorder?

answers: As an estimate only when reliable information exists, without unsupported promises

practical: Given a sample incomplete delivery, identify the exact SKU/quantity shortage, document it on route/office paperwork, explain who must be notified, and describe the electronic and physical records required.

Given sample backordered material that has just arrived, demonstrate RESERVE IT → COMMUNICATE IT → DELIVER IT → CLOSE IT, including staging, priority fulfillment and the condition required before closing the record.
source: Bargain Moulding — SOP: Customer Backorder Management & Resolution, Revision 1.0

title: Cycle Counts & Inventory Discrepancies
summary: Maintain accurate Qoblex inventory through scheduled physical counts, immediate discrepancy investigation, authorized corrections, and verification.
sections: Purpose

Cycle counts are a routine inventory-control process, not a once-a-year cleanup. Each scheduled count should leave the category as accurate as reasonably possible. The first 90 days are a pilot used to establish a reliable counting rhythm and identify categories or SKUs that need more attention.
System of Record

Qoblex is the official inventory system of record. Shopify sales update Qoblex. Material on an unfulfilled customer order may remain physically in the warehouse while Qoblex shows that quantity as allocated. Allocated material is still part of physical on-hand inventory until it is fulfilled.
Ownership

The Warehouse Manager spearheads cycle counts and assigns warehouse employees to perform the physical counts. The Warehouse Manager is responsible for making sure counts happen, verifying discrepancies, and escalating unresolved differences.
Weekly Completion Standard

The scheduled category must be fully counted, discrepancies investigated, approved corrections completed, and results verified within its assigned week. The Warehouse Manager may choose when during the week the work occurs and divide the count among warehouse employees as needed. Physical counting should be performed in concentrated blocks whenever practical to minimize inventory movement during the count. Counts should not be unnecessarily spread across several days. Once a SKU or manageable section is counted, compare and reconcile it promptly so sales, receiving, picking, transfers, and other inventory movement do not create false discrepancies. If normal operations prevent completion, the Warehouse Manager must treat that as an exception and arrange prompt catch-up rather than simply waiting for the next rotation.
Adjustment Authority

Warehouse employees and Warehouse Managers do not change Qoblex quantities simply to make the system match a count. Inventory quantity adjustments are authorized and/or made only by the Inventory Manager and/or Director of Procurement (DOP).
Count Method

When practical, employees should perform a blind physical count without being shown the expected Qoblex quantity first. Count the entire assigned category and every stocked SKU/variant. For moulding profiles stocked in both PRF and MDF, count each variant separately against its respective Qoblex SKU.
Compare Correctly

Compare the confirmed physical quantity to Qoblex On Hand—not merely Available inventory. Example: if Qoblex shows 100 On Hand and 25 Allocated, approximately 100 pieces should physically exist; only 75 are available to sell. Allocation does not remove material from physical inventory.
Discrepancy Investigation

If Physical On Hand does not equal Qoblex On Hand, do not immediately adjust Qoblex. Recount first. Then check the correct SKU/profile/size and material variant, other storage locations, allocated or staged customer material, recent receiving, transfers, returns, damaged material, fulfillment activity, and other reasonable transaction or location issues.
Correct Each Week

Confirmed discrepancies are addressed during the week they are discovered. Do not wait until the end of the 90-day pilot. After reasonable investigation, unresolved true inventory differences are escalated to the Inventory Manager and/or DOP for review and authorized Qoblex correction.
Verify & Learn

After an approved adjustment, verify Qoblex against the confirmed physical count. Record enough information to identify patterns: date, SKU, Qoblex on-hand, physical count, variance, known cause when available, and adjustment/result. A problem SKU may be scheduled for an earlier targeted recount.
Customer Impact

If a discrepancy means material allocated to an existing customer order is no longer physically available, treat it as a customer fulfillment issue and follow the Customer Backorder Management & Resolution SOP. Do not allow an inventory correction to hide an affected customer order.
90-Day Pilot Rotation

Week 1: Base. Week 2: Casing. Week 3: Interior Doors. Week 4: Crown. Week 5: PVC. Week 6: Smalls + Shiplap + S4S Boards. Week 7: Cabinets. Week 8: Flooring. Week 9: Exterior Doors. Week 10: Base second count. Week 11: Casing second count. Week 12: targeted discrepancy recounts/problem SKUs. Week 13: final verification and catch-up counts.
Operating Standard

COUNT → INVESTIGATE → CORRECT → VERIFY → MOVE ON. A scheduled cycle count is not permission to blindly overwrite Qoblex. The goal is accurate inventory today and better information for determining future count frequency.

answers: The count should be stretched across all five days

answers: Follow the Customer Backorder Management & Resolution SOP
Wait for the next cycle count

practical: Assign an employee a sample category/SKU and observe a blind physical count, including separate stocked variants where applicable.
Have the employee explain how they would complete an assigned weekly category in concentrated counting blocks while minimizing inventory movement and reconciling counted sections promptly.

source: Bargain Moulding — Cycle Count & Inventory Discrepancy Policy (90-Day Pilot)

title: Purchase Order Creation & Management
summary: Control every purchase from request through vendor documentation so Qoblex, Receiving, Procurement, and Accounting have a matching purchasing record.
sections: Golden Rule

NO PO → NO PURCHASE. No material may be ordered from a vendor unless the Director of Procurement (DOP) has first created and issued a Purchase Order in Qoblex. Requesting a PO after an order has already been placed is not the normal process.
Why the PO Matters

The Qoblex PO is the official purchasing record. The PO number connects the purchase to vendor documentation, receiving, and the invoice Accounting must reconcile and pay. The documentation chain is Qoblex PO → Vendor Order/BOM → Receiving → Vendor Invoice.
Stock & Standard Inventory Orders

The DOP owns stock and standard inventory purchasing. The DOP creates the PO in Qoblex, places the vendor order, and normally receives the vendor BOM or order confirmation directly. Other employees may not independently place stock inventory orders with vendors.
Customer Special Orders

Certain customer sales require vendor purchasing, including applicable special-order moulding, flex moulding, third-party special-order doors, and cabinet orders. After the counter sale, the appropriate Inside Sales employee or Kitchen Cabinet Specialist receives the POS order information and requests a PO from the DOP. Do not place the vendor order yet.
PO Before Vendor Order
The DOP creates the special-order PO in Qoblex and issues the PO number. Only after the Qoblex PO has been issued may Inside Sales or the Kitchen Cabinet Specialist place the order with the vendor.
Vendor BOM / Order Confirmation

For customer special orders, the vendor may email its BOM or order confirmation to the Inside Sales employee or Kitchen Cabinet Specialist who placed the order. That employee must forward the received BOM/confirmation to the DOP. The DOP acknowledges the documentation and scans/attaches it to the corresponding Qoblex PO. This is a documentation step after the vendor order is placed; it is not a second authorization gate before ordering.
Receiving Handoff

Once purchased material physically arrives at a branch, follow SOP 03 — Receiving Purchase Orders. SOP 03 governs matching the Qoblex PO, vendor packing slip, and physical product; counting and inspection; partial shipments; Qoblex receiving/authorization; and required closeout communication. Material arriving does not automatically mean the entire PO should be closed.
Partial Shipments

Under SOP 03, receive only products physically present and leave remaining quantities open. Never receive material that is not physically present on-site. Follow SOP 03 and notify the DOP as required.
Damaged Material Handoff

Do not receive damaged material as though everything arrived correctly. Follow SOP 03 — Receiving Purchase Orders for the receiving process and SOP 08 — Damaged Material & Claims for damaged-material handling. Photograph the damage, move affected material to HOLD – DAMAGED MATERIAL when practical, notify the DOP, preserve supporting documentation/packaging when applicable, and follow Procurement direction for Qoblex receiving and final disposition.
Related SOPs
SOP 03 — Receiving Purchase Orders. SOP 08 — Damaged Material & Claims. These procedures control the process after purchased material physically arrives and when damage is identified.
Operating Standard
REQUEST → PO → ORDER → DOCUMENT → RECEIVE. Above everything else: NO PO → NO PURCHASE.

answers: Place the order and request a PO afterward

Ask the Branch Manager to create a PO

answers: Forward it to the DOP for Qoblex filing
Wait for the Branch Manager to approve it

answers: Receive 12 and leave the remaining quantity open

quiz.question: Material arrives damaged against a valid PO. What should the employee do?
answers: Receive it as correct because the PO exists
Discard it and close the PO

practical: Given a customer special-order scenario, have the employee explain the sequence from POS order through Qoblex PO issuance and vendor ordering, including the NO PO → NO PURCHASE rule.

source: Bargain Moulding — Purchase Order Creation & Management Policy
